question: Which type of computer processes continuous physical quantities like blood pressure or temperature?
explanation: Analog systems measure continuous physical quantities directly without converting them into discrete numbers first. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T6#GNS113_U1_T6_h1)

question: Why are standard electronic health record terminals classified as digital computers?

options.A: They rely strictly on fluctuating electrical voltages
options.B: They combine analog input with manual calculation
options.C: They process data using discrete binary digits
options.D: They measure continuous physical waves directly

explanation: Digital machines rely on binary code representing discrete numbers and letters to store and manipulate patient records. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T6#GNS113_U1_T6_h1)

question: Besides physical dimensions, what main factor is used to group computers by size and capacity?
explanation: Processing speed alongside physical size and memory capacity determines where a computer falls on the hardware hierarchy scale. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T6#GNS113_U1_T6_h2)

question: How do large enterprise computer systems differ fundamentally from smaller standalone units?

options.A: They are designed strictly for single-user personal documentation
options.B: They operate entirely without electrical power sources
options.C: They handle massive simultaneous data streams for entire hospitals
options.D: They process continuous physical waves instead of binary code

explanation: Large enterprise systems possess the immense processing power needed to coordinate data across multiple hospital departments at once. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T6#GNS113_U1_T6_h2)

question: What is the defining hardware feature of a microcomputer?

options.A: An exclusively analog data processing architecture
options.B: The requirement of a dedicated air-conditioned server room
options.C: The capacity to coordinate national genomic databases
options.D: A central processing unit on a single microprocessor chip

explanation: The integration of the entire CPU onto a single silicon chip is what distinguishes microcomputers from larger architectures. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T6#GNS113_U1_T6_h3)

question: A nurse carrying a portable tablet during ward rounds is primarily utilizing which computer class?
explanation: Handheld tablets and laptops belong to the microcomputer category due to their compact size and microprocessor-based design. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T6#GNS113_U1_T6_h3)

question: What type of computer system supports thousands of users at once to manage hospital-wide databases?
explanation: Mainframes are robust enterprise systems engineered to handle massive workloads and thousands of simultaneous users safely. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T6#GNS113_U1_T6_h4)

question: A hospital department needs a mid-sized server to coordinate laboratory test results across multiple wards. Which system fits best?
explanation: Minicomputers act as midrange servers ideal for handling departmental workloads like laboratory or pharmacy data tracking. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T6#GNS113_U1_T6_h4)

question: What is the primary function of a supercomputer in medical research?

options.A: Processing continuous analog blood pressure waveforms
options.B: Running complex simulations for drug design and genomic sequencing
options.C: Recording routine vital signs on a single medical ward
options.D: Printing daily shift duty rosters at the nurse's station

explanation: Supercomputers are reserved for computationally intensive tasks like genomic analysis and advanced pharmaceutical research. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T6#GNS113_U1_T6_h5)

question: Why are supercomputers rarely found at standard hospital nursing stations?

options.A: Their physical memory is too small to store electronic health records
options.B: They only process analog signals from mechanical thermometers
options.C: Their immense processing power exceeds everyday clinical documentation needs
options.D: They are completely incapable of connecting to digital networks

explanation: Standard nursing tasks require routine data entry, making the extreme processing capabilities of supercomputers unnecessary at the bedside. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T6#GNS113_U1_T6_h5)

question: What happens when a healthcare facility uses underpowered computer hardware for a heavy hospital-wide database?

options.A: The unit transforms into a high-speed supercomputer
options.B: System bottlenecks and operational delays occur
options.C: The computer automatically upgrades its internal memory
options.D: Data processing shifts entirely to analog measurement

explanation: Underpowered hardware struggles to manage heavy data traffic, resulting in slow response times and workflow disruptions. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T6#GNS113_U1_T6_h6)

question: A clinic manager needs a device that balances affordability and mobility for nurses recording vital signs at the bedside. Which choice is most appropriate?
explanation: Tablets provide the ideal mix of portability, cost-effectiveness, and processing power required for bedside clinical documentation. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T6#GNS113_U1_T6_h6)
